epithet: The servants of the Most Merciful
lede: They said: what sort of messenger is this, who eats food and walks in the markets? The surah answers every taunt in turn — and then, in its last fifteen ayat, shows what this Qurʾan makes of the people who take it in. They walk on the earth gently, and when the ignorant address them, they say: peace.

names.name: al-Furqān
names.note: From its first ayah. Ibn al-Jawzī: the Furqān is the Qurʾan, so called because by it truth is parted from falsehood.

revelation.detail: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Mujāhid, ʿIkrimah and Qatādah, among others, said it is Makkan, and al-Qurṭubī calls that the saying of the majority. It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās and Qatādah that three of its ayat (25:68–70) came down in Madinah. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk alone held the reverse. The Companions were already reciting it in the Prophet’s lifetime as a surah by this name: ʿUmar heard Hishām ibn Ḥakīm reciting “Sūrat al-Furqān” in prayer. The traditional order places it forty-second.

evidence.quote: قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ، والحَسَنُ، ومُجاهِدٌ، وعِكْرِمَةُ، وقَتادَةُ في آخَرِينَ: هي مَكِّيَّةٌ. وحُكِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ وقَتادَةَ أنَّهُما قالا: إلّا ثَلاثَ آياتٍ مِنها نَزَلَتْ بِالمَدِينَةِ
وَمَقْصُودُ هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ ذِكْرُ مَوْضِعِ عِظَمِ الْقُرْآنِ، وَذِكْرُ مَطَاعِنِ الْكُفَّارِ فِي النبوة والرد على مقالاتهم

setting: Al-Qurṭubī states what the surah is for: to show the greatness of the Qurʾan, and to set down what the disbelievers said against the prophethood and answer it. It reads like a record of a hearing. Each objection is quoted as it was spoken, and each is met.

This is nothing but a lie he has invented, and others have helped him with it. Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, dictated to him morning and evening. What is the matter with this messenger, that he eats food and walks about the markets? Why has no angel been sent down to be with him as a warner — or a treasure thrown down to him, or a garden he could eat from? You follow only a man bewitched. Why are the angels not sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord? Why was the Qurʾan not sent down to him all at once?

The answers are short. He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth sent it down. We sent no messengers before you but they ate food and walked in the markets. And as for sending it down in parts: “Thus — that We may make your heart firm by it; and We have recited it in measured recitation. They bring you no argument but We bring you the truth and a better explanation.”

Twice the surah lets the Prophet ﷺ see past the argument to its end. The Day the wrongdoer bites his hands and says: “Would that I had taken a path with the Messenger. Woe to me — would that I had not taken so-and-so for a friend.” The commentators relate that this was about ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ, who had begun to listen and was turned back by a friend’s scorn. And then the Messenger’s own complaint, kept in the Qurʾan as he will make it: “My Lord, my people have taken this Qurʾan as a thing abandoned.”
When the Makkans were told to prostrate to al-Raḥmān, they said: “And what is al-Raḥmān?” The close of the surah answers by describing His servants.

occasions.title: The greatest of sins
occasions.text: Ibn Masʿūd said: I asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: “Which sin is greatest with Allah?” He said: “That you set up a rival to Allah, when He created you.” I said: “Then what?” He said: “That you kill your child for fear that he will eat with you.” I said: “Then what?” He said: “That you commit adultery with your neighbour’s wife.” And Allah sent down in confirmation of it: “Those who do not call upon another god with Allah, nor kill the soul Allah has forbidden except by right, nor commit adultery.”
occasions.source: ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd: al-Bukhārī (4761) and Muslim (86).

occasions.title: “If only you told us there is an expiation”
occasions.text: Some people of the idolaters had killed, and killed much, and committed adultery, and done so much. They came to Muḥammad ﷺ and said: “What you say and call to is good — if only you would tell us that there is an expiation for what we have done.” Then there came down: “Those who do not call upon another god with Allah…”, and: “Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah.”

aim: To come to the defence of the Messenger ﷺ, after the idolaters had grown insolent towards him.
themes: The objections to the Messenger, answered
Why the Qurʾan came down in parts
Signs: the shadow, the two seas, night and day
The servants of the Most Merciful
Repentance that turns evil deeds to good

outline.title: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion
outline.summary: Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds — He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has taken no son and has no partner, who created everything and measured it exactly. Those who disbelieve say: “This is only a lie he has invented… tales of the ancients… What is the matter with this messenger, that he eats food and walks in the markets?”

outline.title: Better than what they asked
outline.summary: Blessed is He who, if He willed, could give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and palaces. No — they have denied the Hour, and for those who deny the Hour We have prepared a blaze; when it sees them from afar, they hear its fury and its roar. The Day He gathers them and what they worshipped: “Was it you who misled these servants of Mine?” We sent no messengers before you but they ate food and walked in the markets; and We have made some of you a trial for others: will you be patient?

outline.title: The Day of regret, and the Qurʾan abandoned
outline.summary: Those who do not expect to meet Us say, “Why are the angels not sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?” The Day they see the angels, there will be no good news for the guilty; and We shall turn to what deeds they did and make them scattered dust. The Day the wrongdoer will bite his hands: “Would that I had taken a path with the Messenger.” And the Messenger will say: “My Lord, my people have taken this Qurʾan as abandoned” (25:30). They say, “Why was the Qurʾan not sent down to him all at once?” Thus — to make your heart firm.

outline.title: Those who denied before
outline.summary: We gave Mūsā the Book, and appointed his brother Hārūn as his helper. The people of Nūḥ, when they denied the messengers, We drowned; and ʿĀd, and Thamūd, and the people of al-Rass, and many generations between. When they see you they take you only in mockery: “Is this the one Allah has sent as a messenger?” Have you seen him who takes his own desire as his god? They are only like cattle; no, they are further astray.

outline.title: Signs of the Most Merciful
outline.summary: Have you not seen how your Lord stretches out the shadow? He made the night a garment for you, and sleep a rest. He sends the winds as good news before His mercy. He let the two seas flow, this one fresh and sweet, that one salt and bitter, and set between them a barrier. He created from water a human being. He created the heavens and the earth in six days, then rose over the Throne: the Most Merciful. When it is said to them, “Prostrate to the Most Merciful,” they say, “And what is the Most Merciful?” He made the night and the day follow one another, for whoever wishes to remember or to give thanks.

outline.title: The servants of the Most Merciful
outline.summary: The servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth gently, and when the ignorant address them, say, “Peace”; who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing; who, when they spend, are neither wasteful nor miserly; who do not call on another god with Allah, nor kill, nor commit adultery — except the one who repents, believes and does right: for those, Allah will change their evil deeds into good. Who do not bear false witness; who, reminded of their Lord’s ayat, do not fall deaf and blind at them; who say: “Our Lord, grant us in our spouses and offspring the comfort of our eyes, and make us leaders of the mindful.”

keyAyah.why: The first line of the portrait the surah has been leading to: the answer, in a human life, to “And what is al-Raḥmān?”

virtues.text: ʿUmar said: I heard Hishām ibn Ḥakīm reciting Sūrat al-Furqān in the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in a way other than the way he had taught it to me. I almost leapt on him in the prayer. I brought him to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who had each of us recite, and said to each: “So it was sent down.” Then he said: “This Qurʾan was sent down in seven modes; so recite of it what is easy for you.”
virtues.arabic: إِنَّ هَذَا الْقُرْآنَ أُنْزِلَ عَلَى سَبْعَةِ أَحْرُفٍ فَاقْرَءُوا مَا تَيَسَّرَ مِنْهُ

virtuesNote: The sixtieth ayah is an ayah of prostration.
before: Al-Nūr closed with the manners owed to the Messenger: do not call him as you call one another. Al-Furqān opens with what those who refused him said about him.
after: Al-Furqān ends: “You have denied, so it will be inescapable.” Al-Shuʿarāʾ shows it: seven peoples who denied, and what became of each.
